purpose: A collection shown as cards, after Cloudscape's cards: one card per item, named by its `header` slot, with the item's fields in the default slot. It shares Table's item and selection model — `items`, `trackBy`, `selectedKeys` — so `useCollection` binds it through `cardsProps`, and selection (single or multi, with a visible select-all) survives paging. Four cards a row in a wide container, then three, two and one as the container narrows.
useWhen: Items people recognise by a few fields or a picture rather than compare column by column (applications, templates, environments).
The card form of a list page (`platform/view/card-view`), filtered and paged by `useCollection`.
avoidWhen: Records compared, sorted or scanned across many fields → use `table`.
A fixed marketing grid of features or links → use `card-grid`.
related: use-collection` — filters, pages and selects; `cardsProps` is the binding.
table` — the same collection as rows; same item and selection model.
bestPractices: Put the item's name, as a link to the item, in the `header` slot: it also names the selection control.
Keep each card to a handful of label and value pairs; let `collection-preferences` choose which.
Use `selectionMode="multi"` only when a bulk action exists next to the list.
Pass items typed with your own interface (`Domain[]`): the slots read `item.name` with that type, so never cast `item` in a slot or widen the items to `Record<string, unknown>[]`.
